title: Paving gangs on holiday

blocks.text: The paving contractor's pool shrinks over the holidays: `available[t]` is the number of gangs on day `t`, for every day of the horizon. Each job needs `(days, gangs)` as before and holds its gangs for every day it runs. Days are numbered from 0.

Write `holiday_plan(jobs, available)` in `gang_days.py`. The horizon is `len(available)`. Return each job's start day, chosen so that the last job ends as early as possible. Every instance in the tests has a plan.
The model, with $`J`$ the jobs, $`d_j`$ and $`g_j`$ their days and gangs, $`a_t`$ the gangs on day $`t`$, $`H`$ the horizon and $`G = \max_t a_t`$:

The (gangs) rows are one cumulative constraint of capacity $`G`$ in which the $`G - a_t`$ missing gangs are held by fixed intervals. Group consecutive days with the same $`a_t`$ into one fixed interval each (a run of days is one interval, as long as the run), and add none where $`a_t = G`$. The tests check the plan you return and how early it ends. About twenty lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from ortools.sat.python import cp_model


def holiday_plan(jobs: dict[str, tuple[int, int]], available: list[int]) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Start day of each job under a pool that changes by day, so the last ends as early as possible."""
    horizon, peak = len(available), max(available)
    model = cp_model.CpModel()
    start, intervals, demands = {}, [], []
    for name, (days, need) in jobs.items():
        start[name] = model.new_int_var(0, horizon - days, f"start_{name}")
        intervals.append(model.new_fixed_size_interval_var(start[name], days, f"pave_{name}"))
        demands.append(need)
    first = 0
    for t in range(1, horizon + 1):
        if t == horizon or available[t] != available[first]:
            if available[first] < peak:
                intervals.append(model.new_fixed_size_interval_var(first, t - first, f"away_{first}"))
                demands.append(peak - available[first])
            first = t
    model.add_cumulative(intervals, demands, peak)

    makespan = model.new_int_var(0, horizon, "makespan")
    model.add_max_equality(makespan, [start[name] + days for name, (days, _) in jobs.items()])
    model.minimize(makespan)
    solver = cp_model.CpSolver()
    solver.parameters.num_workers = 1
    solver.solve(model)
    return {name: solver.value(start[name]) for name in jobs}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(holiday_plan({"elm": (3, 2), "oak": (2, 1), "ash": (4, 1)}, [3, 3, 1, 1, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3]))

cases.says: with the same number of gangs every day, the plan ends as early as the pool allows
every job gets a whole-number start day and ends by the horizon
days with fewer gangs hold the work back only on those days; the full pool is used on the others
a run of several days with fewer gangs limits the work on every one of those days
